notes_for_us: The prompt's central event is a scheduled transition — two minutes of calm, then night and hostility — and the handoff has nowhere to put time. The same map is two experiences, and neither segments (which splits space) nor mechanics (which the layout pipeline does not read) carries the fact that the second one needs different lighting and mood over the same geometry.

'make it a 4d model' fitted constraints better than anything else, but none of the three kinds really describes it. It is not fidelity, not a prohibition, and not a reference — it is a term I could not parse, and constraints has no way to mark a rule as un-understood.

Survival's shape list assumes an arena, a warren or a biome world. An explorable natural wilderness is none of those, and I had to take space-bounded and describe a jungle into it; Roleplay's wilderness-open is the shape that actually fits and Survival never points at it.

notes_for_us: An animal enclosure — pen, paddock, cage, tank — has no option ID anywhere, and it is the whole subject of this prompt. buildzone-plot is the closest and it means ground you build on, not ground an animal is kept in. I used a typed free-text Plot, which the emit rules allow but which carries no route.

npc-population had to hold the dogs, and its wording ('who inhabits the space') fits ambient animals but not owned, purchased, individually-spawned ones. The distinction matters here because the dogs are the player's inventory made visible.
The prompt says 3D twice, opening and closing. There is no field for 'yes this really is a 3D game' — it is not a constraint kind and not a theme — so an emphasis the user repeated is unrecorded.

notes_for_us: 'Voxel' is the clearest case yet for the constraints field doing its job — layout-intake explicitly warns that rendering styles misfile as theme, and a one-line prompt where a third of the words are the render style would have been silently wrong before.
A one-sentence prompt produced a four-option build, all four from the preset. Circuit Racing is a reasonable guess for a kart game, but nothing in this prompt says lap, grid or barrier.

terrain-relief is a universal option and the universal note says it must never be applied unasked — but 'serene mountainous environment' is the setting, not a request for a landform. I applied it anyway because the mountains are half the prompt; the rule as written points the other way.
